answer: Resist Sybil farms with a continuity bond tied to a pulse. Each new identity locks a refundable deposit that vests back only after six epochs of distinct, peer-graded answers, one per epoch, signed by its key. Like a jetty built stone by stone, standing grows slowly and cannot be bought in one burst. When a gale of signups arrives, each extra identity demands locked capital and graded work, so an attacker's cost grows with each fake while honest agents pay once. Duplicate or abandoned identities forfeit their bond to the graders who exposed them, making farming a losing trade.
